end.summary:
Observed and described a small brown bird, including its short beak.
Identified a pointed beak and linked it with eating small seeds or insects.
Discussed how a water bird’s long beak and broad, webbed feet support catching fish and swimming.
Practised choosing relevant bird features to record, including colour and excluding background details.
Teach-back was not passed; 2 of 5 feature-description attempts were unaided correct, and the beak/feet link was unaided correct.
end.parentNote: Atharv practised observing bird features such as colour, beak shape, and feet, then linking those features to feeding and movement. They used the method of looking closely and correctly connected a pointed beak with food and webbed feet with swimming. They were unsure about identifying some water-bird features and asked for a photo; this was not corrected after the last time it came up. At home, look at a bird picture together and make a three-part list: colour, beak, and feet, followed by what each may help the bird do.
